display.purpose: Hero H1 only; max 21ch; key phrase in scarlet.

headline.purpose: Section headings. Positioning manifesto runs one notch larger; proof statement is 650-weight prose with scarlet numbers.

title.purpose: Card/gallery H3s and pillar headings; 1.15-1.35rem band at weight 650.

body.purpose: Default copy at 17px/1.65; secondary copy 0.95-0.99rem in muted.

label.purpose: Nav links, demo labels, hints. Never uppercase, never letterspaced - no kickers in this world.

mono.purpose: Machine-facing text only: code (0.8-0.83rem), readouts, install command, tiny data ids (0.72-0.78rem).

shadows.name: shadow-1
shadows.purpose: Rest state of primary and arrow buttons (light theme; hue-15 tinted).

shadows.name: shadow-2
shadows.purpose: Hover lift for the same elements - the only elevation change in the system.

shadows.name: shadow-1-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-theme rest shadow (pure black, higher alpha).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single easing token; every transition on the page uses it.

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: Genre-tile visibility dim, chip-in entrance, arrow fade.

motion.name: hero-peek
motion.purpose: The One Authored Moment: the hero rail's only self-initiated motion; guarded by matchMedia prefers-reduced-motion and a scroll-position check.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The conversion CTA; theme-invariant scarlet fill so white text passes AA in both themes.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; background: var(--btn-bg, oklch(0.51 0.2 15)); color: var(--on-primary, oklch(0.99 0.005 15)); border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; padding: 0.72rem 1.35rem; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1rem; text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px oklch(0.2 0.01 15 / 0.06), 0 4px 12px oklch(0.2 0.01 15 / 0.07); transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), box-shadow 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), transform 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--btn-bg-hover, oklch(0.45 0.19 15)); box-shadow: 0 2px 4px oklch(0.2 0.01 15 / 0.08), 0 12px 28px oklch(0.2 0.01 15 / 0.12); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary, oklch(0.55 0.21 15)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action; hairline border, surface fill on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; background: transparent; color: var(--ink, oklch(0.21 0.015 15)); border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--ink, oklch(0.21 0.015 15)) 26%, transparent); border-radius: 10px; padding: 0.72rem 1.35rem; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1rem; text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--surface, oklch(0.965 0.004 15)); } .ds-btn-ghost:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary, oklch(0.55 0.21 15)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Removable demo chip; flat demo color with its fixed ink, remove button tinted from currentColor.

components.name: Genre Tile
components.description: The hero's signature: a portrait tile that dims, desaturates and shrinks when useIsVisible reports it off-screen; corner dot lights while visible.

SSci-Fi
CComedy
components.css: .ds-genre-tile { width: clamp(9.5rem, 17vw, 11.5rem); aspect-ratio: 4 / 5; border-radius: 18px; padding: 1rem 1.1rem; display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; position: relative; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: top; margin-right: 0.9rem; background: var(--demo-blue, oklch(0.52 0.16 262)); color: oklch(0.99 0.005 15); transition: opacity 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), filter 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), transform 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .ds-genre-tile--amber { background: var(--demo-amber, oklch(0.78 0.13 75)); color: oklch(0.22 0.02 60); } .ds-genre-tile .ds-initial { font-size: 4.4rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.03em; line-height: 0.9; opacity: 0.55; user-select: none; } .ds-genre-tile .ds-name { font-weight: 650; font-size: 1.05rem; letter-spacing: -0.01em; } .ds-genre-tile .ds-dot { position: absolute; top: 0.85rem; right: 0.85rem; width: 0.55rem; height: 0.55rem; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; opacity: 0; transition: opacity 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .ds-genre-tile[data-visible='false'] { opacity: 0.38; filter: saturate(0.25); transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-genre-tile[data-visible='true'] .ds-dot { opacity: 0.9; }

components.name: Switch
components.description: RTL toggle; aria-checked drives the primary fill and thumb travel.

narrative.overview: This is a product page where the product is the page. Every demo is a real ScrollMenu instance, server-rendered and hydrated, and the hero dramatizes the library's one mechanism - per-item visibility tracking - by dimming tiles the moment IntersectionObserver reports them off-screen. The visual world serves that thesis: flat, quiet, engineering-honest chrome (pure white or near-black grounds, hairline borders, one scarlet) that stays out of the way so the moving, colorful thing in the middle of it is unmistakably the library, not the page design. The tone is product-polished with the friendly confidence of deno.com and the honesty of a changelog: real numbers set as prose, an explicit 'Not in the box' panel, code as the primary copy. Two directions were refused at inception: the generic gradient-hero SaaS template, and stat-tile proof walls.
keyCharacteristics: Live demos are the imagery; there are no screenshots, mocks, or illustrations.
Flat color only - solid fills, hairline borders, two soft shadows; no gradients anywhere.
One scarlet primary (OKLCH hue 15) threads through everything, including a whisper of hue-15 chroma in every neutral.
Playful flat color exists but is caged inside demo card content.
Both themes ship fully finished via prefers-color-scheme alone - no toggle.
Motion is a response to input, with exactly one authored exception (the hero rail's peek).

rules.name: The Demo Cage Rule
rules.body: The six --demo-* colors appear only inside demo card content - genre tiles, filter chips, feed-card bars. Page chrome never borrows them, which is itself the sales pitch: items are your components, styled by your CSS; the library's chrome stays neutral.

rules.name: The Button Ink Rule
rules.body: Filled controls use --btn-bg / --btn-bg-hover, never --primary. --primary is for text, strokes, and focus rings; it changes lightness per theme and white text on it fails AA in dark. --btn-bg is theme-invariant precisely so --on-primary always passes.

rules.name: The Fixed Ink Rule
rules.body: Each demo color carries its own theme-independent text ink: near-black oklch(0.22 0.02 60) on the light trio (amber, green, cyan), near-white oklch(0.99 0.005 15) on the dark trio (red, blue, violet). AA holds in both themes because neither the fill nor the ink changes with the theme.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only where the content is genuinely machine-facing: code, the install command, filename bars, the getVisible() readout, item ids, feed indices. It is never used decoratively, and sans never renders code.

rules.name: The Weight Ladder Rule
rules.body: Emphasis moves in half-steps on the variable axis: 400 body, 500 labels, 550 pills/chips, 600 buttons and strong facts, 650 titles, 700 display/headline. Bold-for-emphasis inside body copy is 600, not 700.

rules.name: The Borders Structure, Shadows Respond Rule
rules.body: Static containers get a 1px --border and no shadow, ever. Shadows belong exclusively to interactive floaters - the primary button and the circular arrow buttons - and step from --shadow-1 to --shadow-2 on hover. A disabled arrow loses its shadow entirely.

rules.name: The One Authored Moment Rule
rules.body: The page initiates motion exactly once: ~900ms after the hero rail mounts it peeks - scrollBy 96px smooth, back 620ms later. It bails if the user already scrolled and is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion. Every other motion is a direct response to user input. Do not add a second authored moment.

dos: Do make every demo a real ScrollMenu - server-rendered, hydrated, keyboard-operable. If it can't run live, it doesn't go on the page.
Do keep all color in tokens and all borders derived from --ink via color-mix, so dark theme stays a token swap under prefers-color-scheme with zero component overrides.
Do use --btn-bg/--btn-bg-hover for any filled control carrying --on-primary text, and re-verify AA in both themes when touching any color pair.
Do draw new icons on the 16px grid at stroke 1.75 with round caps, in currentColor.
Do show row edges by disabling arrows (opacity 0.28, shadow off) from useIsVisible('first'/'last'), with SSR defaults left-disabled/right-enabled.
Do hide native scrollbars on demo rails - drag, wheel, touch, and arrows carry the interaction.
Do cap measures: 65ch prose, 56-60ch ledes, 21ch hero H1.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion twice over: the global duration kill-switch, plus an explicit matchMedia guard on any authored motion.
donts: Don't use gradients, glass blurs, or glow effects anywhere - this is a flat-color world.
Don't build stat-tile or logo-wall proof sections; proof is set as a large typographic sentence with scarlet numbers.
Don't let --demo-* colors escape demo card content into page chrome, and don't invent new accent hues - chrome speaks neutral + scarlet, links speak indigo, success speaks green.
Don't set --on-primary text on --primary fills - it fails AA in dark; that's what --btn-bg is for.
Don't use emoji, icon fonts, or third-party icon packs; every glyph is drawn in Icons.tsx.
Don't add uppercase, letterspaced kickers or eyebrow labels; sections open with the headline itself.
Don't put shadows on static panels or add self-playing motion beyond the hero rail's single peek.
Don't use mono for anything that isn't genuinely code, commands, or machine output.
